title: Quarterly Activation Framework: Private Tenant Feature Wave & Hypothesis Registry
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Objective: Define and operationalize a repeatable quarterly activation framework for Private/VPC/on-prem feature waves that pairs a hypothesis registry with tranche-based rollouts. The framework will reduce time-to-first-customer activation, provide measurable OKR-aligned signals, and minimize rollback risk for features that require customer-side networking or on-prem changes.

Why now: Several early enterprise customers are requesting faster, lower-friction activation of Private features (RBAC, KMS integrations, upgrade windows). Current onboarding is ad-hoc, leading to missed SLAs and inconsistent telemetry. This initiative scopes the product, ops, and release guardrails needed across Q2->Q3.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Create a hypothesis registry schema (prompt sets, compatibility matrix, success criteria) and wire it into the release cadence.
- Define 3 tranche cohorts (Lighthouse, Early Access, Broad) with explicit gating criteria and expected metrics.
- Establish the acceptance signal set (safety, performance, security) and dashboards for go/no-go decisions.
- Build a rollout playbook template that Solutions Eng and CSMs can customize for tenant activation.
- Document rollback and mitigation patterns for on-prem network failures and KMS mismatches.

Out of scope: Implementation of specific infra automation (captured in ENG epics), and long-term billing changes. This ticket focuses on product definition, gating metrics, templates, and cross-functional runbook ownership.

Success criteria (aligned to OKRs):
- OKR 1.1: Reduce median Private tenant activation time from 21 days to 10 days for Lighthouse cohort.
- OKR 1.2: Keep activation rollback rate < 5% across Early Access cohort.
- OKR 2.1: All tranche activations publish a hypothesis card and associated prompt/regression tests before canary.
- Operational: Dashboard with live signals (latency P50/P95, quota usage, auth errors) available to SRE and SE within the activation window.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Customer network topologies vary widely -> Mitigation: Pre-activation connectivity checklist + scripted diagnostics for common NAT/firewall patterns.
- Risk: KMS/HSM configuration mismatch -> Mitigation: Add KMS sanity checks to onboarding playbook and require test key exchange for Lighthouse.
- Risk: Rollout causes token-cost spikes -> Mitigation: Quota caps + temporary throttling rules per tranche.

Deliverables by tranche:
- Lighthouse (small trust customers): Hypothesis card + step-by-step playbook + dedicated SE liaison. Gate: Success on 3 connectivity and 2 perf signals.
- Early Access (~10 customers): Automated connectivity diagnostics + preflight runbook + limited-auto-scaling policy. Gate: <5% rollback, perf within SLO.
- Broad (>50 customers): Self-serve activation template + operator-run dashboards + billing/quotas enabled. Gate: Runbook validated and SE support overhead documented.

Stakeholder asks for initial sync (week 0):
- Eng: Confirm the minimal automation required for Early Access gating (ENG-22114).
- SRE: Review control-plane telemetry necessary for go/no-go gates.
- Sales/CS: Identify 3 lighthouse customers willing to pilot (target list attached).
- Legal/Security: Confirm contract addenda needed for on-prem keys.

Implementation notes (product trade-offs):
- Trade-off: Automated preflight diagnostics increase cadence time but reduce on-site SE effort. Decision: prioritize diagnostics for Early Access and automate portions of Lighthouse to reduce manual steps.
- Trade-off: Tighter rollout gating reduces risk but increases engineering gating friction. Decision: Use canary+metric guardrails and allow product exceptions with documented compensating controls.

Next steps (owner: Nina):
1) Finalize hypothesis registry fields and publish template (due 2026-03-08).
2) Workshop gating metrics with SRE and Eng (due 2026-03-12).
3) Produce the activation playbook v0 and circulate to SE/CS (due 2026-03-22).
